motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Default easing for hovers, tilts, lifts and underline grows (expo-out character).

motion.name: ease-curtain
motion.purpose: The intro overlay's 0.7s clip-path lift (overlay removed 750ms after).

motion.name: intro-timing
motion.value: playbackRate 2.2; lift when film time >= 3.6s and page loaded; safety cap 4000ms
motion.purpose: Keeps the once-per-session intro short (about 2.7s on a local load).

motion.name: section-rise
motion.value: y 70px, rotateX -18deg to 0, 1.1s expo.out, stagger 0.1s, at 82% viewport
motion.purpose: Section entrances by position and tilt; content is never hidden by opacity.

motion.name: hero-recede
motion.value: --recede 0 to 1 scrubbed over the hero: translateY -70px, translateZ -280px, rotateX +16deg, rotateY -26deg
motion.purpose: The hero window stack pulls back in depth as the page scrolls.

motion.name: pointer-tilt
motion.value: hero stack rotateY -16deg +/- 11deg, rotateX 8deg +/- 7deg; work panels up to 8deg Y, 6deg X; 0.5 to 0.6s transition
motion.purpose: Depth answers the pointer on fine-pointer devices only.

motion.name: smooth-scroll
motion.value: Lenis lerp 0.1, driven by the GSAP ticker; anchor scroll 1.4s
motion.purpose: Ties scroll-scrubbed effects together; stopped during the intro.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: all transitions 0.01ms; no GSAP; field renders one still frame; ring and intro skipped
motion.purpose: The page reads complete and still.

narrative.overview:
The site is a dark room lit by two lights. A near-black ground holds graphite panels; ember orange is the warm key light and the only colour an action is ever filled with; the logo's cobalt is the cool second light that draws lines, rims and the low end of the hero's point field. Depth is the material: real product windows float at three distances in CSS 3D, tilt toward the pointer and recede as the page scrolls, work panels tilt with a white glare, and every raised panel is edged by a one-pixel rim that runs from cobalt in one corner to ember in the other.

Type is squared and loud. Chakra Petch in uppercase carries every heading at poster scale with tight leading (0.88 to 0.92); Manrope carries reading text at a generous 18px. Words that matter sit on ember highlighter bars rather than changing colour. Layout runs edge to edge: there is no max-width container, only a fluid gutter, so the hero and every section share one left edge at any width.

Motion moves things through space, not in and out of visibility. Sections arrive by rising and untilting; a statement band crosses out the old tools line by line as it scrolls; a ring of stack names turns and lights the matching row of the list beside it. Smooth scroll ties it together. Under reduced motion all of it stops, and the page reads complete and still.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black ground, graphite panels, ember as the single action fill with dark text on it.
Cobalt as the cool counter-light: rims, progress lines, the point field, secondary labels.
Uppercase Chakra Petch display at poster scale; Manrope 18px body with tabular numerals.
Square corners everywhere; depth from perspective, rim light and one deep black drop shadow.
Full-bleed sections with a clamp gutter; no centred max-width column.
Motion is position, tilt and depth; reduced motion freezes everything into a complete static page.

rules.name: The One Fill Rule
rules.body: Ember is the only colour a clickable thing is filled with, and its text is always On-Ember. Cobalt never fills a control.

rules.name: The Two Lights Rule
rules.body: Colour light enters only through the rim, the point field and lines: cobalt from one side, ember from the other. There are no coloured blurred glows, no gradient text and no glass cards.

rules.name: The Uppercase Display Rule
rules.body: Every Chakra Petch heading is uppercase, 700, letter-spacing -0.01em, line-height under 1.05. The statement paragraph is the one sentence-case display use.

rules.name: The Highlighter Rule
rules.body: Emphasis inside display type is an ember bar behind the word (On-Ember text, bar at 0.84em height), wiped in from the left. Never a colour change or gradient on the letters.

rules.name: The Two-Light Rim Rule
rules.body: Raised panels (product windows, work panels, facts, steps) take a 1px transparent border filled by a border-box gradient at an angle: cobalt, faint bone (8%) from 38% to 62%, then ember. On work panels the angle turns so the cobalt corner faces the pointer. This rim is the only coloured light on a panel.

rules.name: The Recede Rule
rules.body: The hero's window stack tilts toward the pointer at rest and, as the hero scrolls out, pulls back up to 280px in depth and turns away. Depth answers the visitor; it never loops on its own.

dos: Do fill every action with Ember (#FF6B35) and set its text in On-Ember (#08090D); hover to Ember Deep (#E8541E).
Do edge raised panels with the two-light rim: 1px transparent border, border-box gradient cobalt, faint bone at 38 to 62%, ember.
Do set headings in uppercase Chakra Petch 700 at -0.01em with line-height 0.88 to 1.05, and emphasise words with the ember highlighter bar.
Do keep corners square (0px) on every control and panel.
Do run sections full bleed inside the clamp(16px, 4vw, 72px) gutter so all content shares one left edge.
Do bring sections in by position and tilt (rise about 70px, untilt from -18 degrees, expo-out over 1.1s) with content fully visible from the first frame.
Do pause continuous effects (wave field, stack ring) when offscreen, and make every effect static under reduced motion.
Do size hero type and the hero CTA by min(vw, vh) so the action stays in the first viewport on short wide screens.
donts: Don't fill controls with cobalt or put white text on ember.
Don't add coloured blurred glows, gradient text or glassmorphism cards; colour light comes only from the rim, the field and lines.
Don't add kickers or eyebrow labels above headings.
Don't number sections; the 01 to 04 process numerals are the only numbering.
Don't use side-stripe accents on cards or rounded corners anywhere.
Don't use any shadow other than the black Deep Drop, and only for objects floating in depth.
Don't use Intro Navy (#000631) outside the intro film overlay.
